easy.def: To make the sound a duck makes.
examples: The duck quacks.
The ducks quacked.
I heard it quack.

more.def: To make the loud, flat sound that a duck makes.
examples: The ducks quacked as we fed them bread.
A duck quacked from the pond.
The toy duck quacks when you squeeze it.
I heard a quack.
The quack was loud.
The duck's quack is funny.

more.def: The loud, flat cry of a duck.
examples: We heard a quack from behind the reeds.
The duck gave a loud quack.
A quack echoed over the pond.

easy.def: A small, plump bird that lives on the ground.
examples: A quail ran across the path.
The quail has a fat body.
We saw a quail with her chicks.

more.def: A small, round bird with a short tail that nests and feeds on the ground.
examples: A quail and her chicks scurried across the road.
The quail ran through the grass instead of flying.
Quails hide in bushes when danger is near.
The ground quaked.
I quake with fear.
The leaves quaked.

more.def: To shake or tremble, as the ground does in an earthquake or as a person does from fear.
examples: The ground quaked beneath our feet during the earthquake.
The little mouse quaked with fear.
His voice quaked when he began to speak.
We felt a quake.
The quake was small.
A quake shook the town.

more.def: A shaking of the ground, short for earthquake.
examples: A small quake rattled the dishes in the kitchen.
The quake lasted only a few seconds.
The town felt a strong quake in the night.

easy.def: The skills or training that make you right for a job.
examples: She has the right qualifications.
His qualifications are great.
What are your qualifications?

more.def: The skills, training or tests that make a person right for a job or a position.
examples: The new teacher has all the right qualifications for the job.
A lifeguard needs special qualifications, such as a swimming test.
The list of qualifications was posted on the door.
She is a qualified nurse.
The teacher is qualified.
He is qualified for the job.

more.def: Having the right training or skills for a job.
examples: Only a qualified electrician should fix the wiring.
The teacher is well qualified to teach math.
He is qualified to drive a bus.

easy.def: To be good enough to enter.
examples: I qualify for the race.
She qualified for the finals.
He qualified.

more.def: To meet the rules or skill needed to take part in something.
examples: I qualified for the swim finals.
She qualifies for a free lunch.
Only the top ten runners qualify for the final.

easy.def: How good or bad something is.
examples: This is a good quality toy.
The quality of the picture is good.
The shoes are high quality.

more.def: How good something is, or a feature that makes a person or thing what they are.
examples: The quality of the photo was very sharp.
Honesty is a quality that many people admire.
This chair is of good quality and will last for years.
A large quantity of food.
The quantity is small.
What quantity do you need?

more.def: The amount or number of something.
examples: A large quantity of food was ready.
The recipe calls for a small quantity of salt.
What quantity of paint do we need?
The sisters had a quarrel about a toy.
The quarrel made them both sad.
They had a quarrel over the swing.

more.def: An angry disagreement between people.
examples: After their quarrel, the two friends said sorry to each other.
The brothers ended their quarrel with a handshake.
A quarrel broke out over whose turn it was.

easy.def: A big pit where stone is dug out of the ground.
examples: Stone comes from a quarry.
We saw a quarry.
The quarry is deep.

more.def: A large pit from which stone, such as granite or limestone, is cut or dug out of the ground; also an animal that is hunted.
examples: Workers cut big blocks of stone from the quarry.
The quarry was a deep pit with sheer walls.
The hawk circled high above, looking for its quarry.

easy.def: A way to measure milk or water; four make a gallon.
examples: Mom bought a quart of milk.
We need a quart of juice.
Pour one quart of water.

more.def: A unit for measuring liquid in the U.S., equal to two pints or one quarter of a gallon.
examples: The recipe needs a quart of milk, which is the same as four cups.
Four quarts of water fill a one-gallon jug.
She drank a whole quart of juice at the picnic.
I ate a quarter of the pie.
Cut the apple in quarters.
A quarter is a fourth.

more.def: One of four equal parts that make a whole.
examples: A quarter of the class has red hair.
The game is divided into four quarters.
Add a quarter of a cup of milk.
I have a quarter.
A quarter is a coin.
I put a quarter in the machine.

more.def: A coin worth twenty-five cents, or one fourth of a dollar.
examples: Four quarters make one dollar.
He found a shiny quarter under the couch.
I paid for the sticker with a quarter.

easy.def: A football player who leads the team's plays.
examples: The quarterback threw the ball.
He is the quarterback.
The quarterback ran.

more.def: The player in American football who throws the ball and directs the team's plays.
examples: The quarterback threw a long pass.
He is the quarterback on our team.
The quarterback called the play.

easy.def: A group of four people who sing or play music together.
examples: The quartet sang.
A string quartet.
Four singers make a quartet.

more.def: A group of four singers or players, or a piece of music for four.
examples: The string quartet played a lovely song at the wedding.
A quartet of four friends sang in the choir.
The piece was written for a quartet.
I feel queasy in the car.
The boat made me queasy.
She felt queasy.

more.def: Feeling as if you might be sick to your stomach.
examples: I feel queasy when I read in the car.
The rocking boat made me queasy.
She felt queasy after eating too much cake.

easy.def: A woman who rules a country.
examples: The queen wore a crown.
The queen lives in a castle.
The queen waved.

more.def: A woman who rules a country, or the wife of a king.
examples: The queen waved to the crowd.
In the fairy tale, the queen wore a golden crown.
The queen and king ruled together.
The queen can move far.
She captured the queen.
Protect your queen.

more.def: In chess, the strongest piece, which can move any number of squares.
examples: In chess, the queen can move in any direction.
He lost his queen early in the game.
She moved her queen across the board.

easy.def: The big bee that lays eggs.
examples: The queen bee lays eggs.
Bees follow the queen.
The hive has one queen.

more.def: The large female in a colony of bees or ants, who lays all the eggs.
examples: Each hive has one queen that lays thousands of eggs.
Worker bees feed the queen.
The queen ant stays in the nest.
The knight went on a quest.
The quest was long.
The hero's quest for gold.

more.def: A long search for something, as in stories.
examples: The knight went on a quest for a magic sword.
The hero's quest took many months.
Their quest was to find the lost treasure.
I have a question. What is your name?
Ask a question if you need help.
That is a good question.

more.def: A sentence you say or write when you want to find something out.
examples: Her question about the moon made the whole class think.
The last question on the test was the hardest.
The reporter asked the mayor a question.

easy.def: Not sure to be right or good.
examples: The answer is questionable.
A questionable idea.
His story is questionable.

more.def: Doubtful, so that you are not sure it is true, right or good.
examples: His story about the missing cookie sounded questionable.
It is questionable whether the old bridge is safe.
The chef had a questionable idea for the dessert: peanut butter pizza.
A rabbit is quick.
Take a quick look.
She gave a quick wave.

more.def: Moving fast, or taking only a short time.
examples: The fox is quick and hard to catch.
Let's take a quick break and then keep going.
She gave him a quick hug before running to class.
The rabbit ran quickly.
Get dressed quickly!
The ice melted quickly.

more.def: Fast; in a short amount of time.
examples: She quickly finished her homework so she could play outside.
News of the win spread quickly.
The nurse quickly put a bandage on the cut.

easy.def: Wet, loose sand that you can sink into.
examples: He stepped in quicksand.
Quicksand is soft.
The explorer avoided the quicksand.

more.def: Soft, wet sand that you can sink into if you step on it, so that it is hard to get out.
examples: In the movie, the explorer stepped into quicksand and had to be pulled out.
Quicksand is wet sand that looks solid but is soft.
Stay on the path to keep away from quicksand.
Please be quiet. The baby is sleeping.
The house is quiet at night.
A mouse is a quiet animal.

more.def: Making little or no noise; calm and still.
examples: The library was so quiet that I could hear the clock ticking.
We live on a quiet street.
He is a quiet boy who loves to draw.
She spoke quietly.
The cat walked quietly.
We sat quietly.

more.def: In a way that makes little or no sound.
examples: The class read quietly for twenty minutes.
The mouse crept quietly across the floor.
He closed the door quietly so he would not wake the baby.
Do not quit. Keep trying!
It is time to quit playing and eat.
He quit the game.

more.def: To stop doing something or to give up.
examples: He wanted to quit the puzzle, but his sister helped him finish.
She quit the team to have more time for music.
The old car quit running halfway up the hill.
It is quite cold today.
The cake was quite big.
She runs quite fast.

more.def: To a fairly large degree; more than a little.
examples: The museum was quite crowded on Saturday afternoon.
It took quite a long time to walk up the mountain.
He was quite sure that he had seen a fox in the garden.

easy.def: A person who gives up too easily.
examples: Do not be a quitter.
He is not a quitter.
A quitter gives up.

more.def: A person who gives up easily instead of trying again.
examples: She is no quitter and kept practicing until she could ride the bike.
A good team does not call anyone a quitter.
He did not want to be a quitter, so he tried again.
The leaf quivers in the wind.
My lip quivers when I am sad.
The jelly quivers on the plate.

more.def: To shake with small, fast movements.
examples: The rabbit's nose quivered as it sniffed the air.
The puppy quivered with excitement.
Her voice quivered as she began her speech.
We have a quiz.
The quiz was easy.
I passed the quiz.

more.def: A short test with a few questions.
examples: We had a math quiz on Friday.
The pop quiz covered the last chapter.
I got every question right on the quiz.

easy.def: To repeat the exact words that someone said.
examples: I quote the teacher.
She quoted a poem.
He quoted the book.

more.def: To repeat the exact words of someone else, in speech or writing.
examples: She quoted a line from her favorite poem.
The reporter quoted the mayor.
He quoted the book in his report.

easy.def: Words that you repeat from someone else.
examples: I read a quote from the book.
The quote is from a poem.
She wrote down a quote.

more.def: A part of a book, speech or poem that is repeated word for word.
examples: The speech began with a quote from a famous poet.
She wrote her favorite quote on the board.
The quote was from a book about space.
